1	package indexroom
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6		"testing"
7	)
8	
9	// This file is the regression guard for running an excludeInstanceIds
10	// selection after the service's instance list has been REPLACED: the
11	// per-service rotation cursor intentionally survives the replacement, so a
12	// selection carrying an exclude list must continue just after the last
13	// actually rotated id — even when that id was removed by the replacement —
14	// instead of restarting at the smallest id. The exclusion itself stays scoped
15	// to its one request: it neither degrades the excluded instance's health
16	// record nor removes it from the service. These tests lock the contract
17	// purely through the public Validate/Apply/Select and Snapshot results:
18	//
19	//   - with a, b, c, d healthy and the cursor resting on b, replacing the list
20	//     (removing b, keeping every other id and address) leaves the position on
21	//     the removed b: excluding c chooses d, the next plain selection wraps to
22	//     a, and the one after chooses the previously excluded c;
23	//   - every successful pick reports the post-replacement revision and the
24	//     address and accepted health sequence of the instance actually chosen;
25	//   - the replacement keeps the surviving instances' health records, and the
26	//     exclude request changes none of them;
27	//   - the instance submission order, in the original registration and in the
28	//     replacement, does not change the selection results;
29	//   - a selection using the pre-replacement revision is a conflict naming
30	//     both revisions, and excluding every healthy instance is no_healthy
31	//     naming the exclusion; both failures report the current revision,
32	//     fabricate no target, and move no cursor, so the next valid selection
33	//     continues just after the last actually rotated id.
34	
35	// runReplaceExcludeScenario drives the shared replacement-plus-exclusion
36	// scenario against a fresh registry with the given instance submission orders
37	// and locks the full pick sequence and the final service state.
38	func runReplaceExcludeScenario(t *testing.T, initial, replacement []Instance) {
39		t.Helper()
40		r := NewRegistry()
41		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, initial)
42		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 11, true, "")
43		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 12, true, "")
44		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 13, true, "")
45		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "d", 1, 14, true, "")
46	
47		// Ordinary selections take a then b; the cursor rests on b.
48		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 11)
49		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "b", "h2:2", 12)
50	
51		// Replace the list at the current revision: b is removed, every other
52		// instance keeps its id and address. The replacement bumps the revision.
53		reg, err := r.ValidateRegistration("svc", 1, replacement)
54		if err != nil {
55			t.Fatalf("validate replacement: %v", err)
56		}
57		if out := r.Apply(reg); !out.OK || !out.Changed || out.Revision != 2 {
58			t.Fatalf("replacement must succeed and bump the revision to 2: %+v", out)
59		}
60	
61		// assertPickRev additionally locks that the pick reports the
62		// post-replacement revision, not the stale pre-replacement one.
63		assertPickRev := func(out SelectOutcome, id, addr string, seq int64) {
64			t.Helper()
65			assertPick(t, out, id, addr, seq)
66			if out.Revision != 2 {
67				t.Fatalf("select must report the post-replacement revision 2, got %+v", out)
68			}
69		}
70	
71		// Excluding c continues just after the removed b: d is chosen with its own
72		// address and accepted sequence. The position neither restarts at the
73		// smallest id (a) nor skips to the excluded c.
74		assertPickRev(selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 2, nil, "c"), "d", "h4:4", 14)
75		// A plain selection wraps past the end to a, and the one after chooses c:
76		// the exclusion was scoped to its one request and never removed c from the
77		// rotation.
78		assertPickRev(selected(t, r, "svc", 2), "a", "h1:1", 11)
79		assertPickRev(selected(t, r, "svc", 2), "c", "h3:3", 13)
80	
81		// The exclusion changed nothing durable: the revision is the replaced one,
82		// b is gone, and the surviving instances keep the health records accepted
83		// before the replacement — c in particular is still healthy at sequence 13.
84		if rev := r.RevisionOf("svc"); rev != 2 {
85			t.Fatalf("revision after replacement: %d", rev)
86		}
87		views := r.Snapshot()
88		if len(views) != 1 || views[0].Service != "svc" || views[0].Revision != 2 {
89			t.Fatalf("service view: %+v", views)
90		}
91		want := []InstanceView{
92			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1", Health: HealthHealthy, Sequence: 11},
93			{ID: "c", Address: "h3:3", Health: HealthHealthy, Sequence: 13},
94			{ID: "d", Address: "h4:4", Health: HealthHealthy, Sequence: 14},
95		}
96		if len(views[0].Instances) != len(want) {
97			t.Fatalf("instances: %+v", views[0].Instances)
98		}
99		for i := range want {
100			if views[0].Instances[i] != want[i] {
101				t.Fatalf("instance %d: got %+v want %+v", i, views[0].Instances[i], want[i])
102			}
103		}
104	}
105	
106	// TestRegistrySelectExcludeAfterReplacementKeepsRotation locks the main
107	// scenario: the exclude-carrying selection after the replacement continues
108	// the rotation from the removed b rather than restarting, and the exclusion
109	// leaves no durable trace. The whole scenario runs under two different
110	// instance submission orders — for the original registration and for the
111	// replacement — and must produce the identical pick sequence, because the
112	// rotation runs by ascending id, never by submission order.
113	func TestRegistrySelectExcludeAfterReplacementKeepsRotation(t *testing.T) {
114		orders := []struct {
115			initial     []Instance
116			replacement []Instance
117		}{
118			{
119				initial: []Instance{
120					{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"},
121					{ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"}, {ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"},
122				},
123				replacement: []Instance{
124					{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"}, {ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"},
125				},
126			},
127			{
128				initial: []Instance{
129					{ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"},
130					{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
131				},
132				replacement: []Instance{
133					{ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"}, {ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
134				},
135			},
136		}
137		for i, tc := range orders {
138			t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("submission order %d", i+1), func(t *testing.T) {
139				runReplaceExcludeScenario(t, tc.initial, tc.replacement)
140			})
141		}
142	}
143	
144	// TestRegistrySelectExcludeFailuresAfterReplacementKeepPosition locks the
145	// failure shapes after the replacement and their effect on the position: a
146	// selection carrying the pre-replacement revision conflicts with both
147	// revisions, and a correct-revision selection excluding every healthy
148	// instance is no_healthy with a reason naming the exclusion. Both report the
149	// current revision and fabricate no target id, address or sequence, and
150	// neither moves the cursor — the next valid selection continues just after
151	// the last actually rotated id.
152	func TestRegistrySelectExcludeFailuresAfterReplacementKeepPosition(t *testing.T) {
153		r := NewRegistry()
154		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
155			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"},
156			{ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"}, {ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"},
157		})
158		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 11, true, "")
159		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 12, true, "")
160		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 13, true, "")
161		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "d", 1, 14, true, "")
162	
163		// The cursor rests on b, which the replacement then removes.
164		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 11)
165		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "b", "h2:2", 12)
166		registerService(t, r, "svc", 1, []Instance{
167			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"}, {ID: "d", Address: "h4:4"},
168		})
169	
170		assertNoTarget := func(out SelectOutcome) {
171			t.Helper()
172			if out.InstanceID != "" || out.Address != "" || out.Sequence != 0 {
173				t.Fatalf("failed select must fabricate no target, got id=%q addr=%q seq=%d",
174					out.InstanceID, out.Address, out.Sequence)
175			}
176		}
177	
178		// A caller still using the pre-replacement revision gets a conflict that
179		// states the expected and actual revisions and reports the current one.
180		sel, err := r.ValidateSelection("svc", 1)
181		if err != nil {
182			t.Fatalf("validate stale-revision select: %v", err)
183		}
184		out := r.Select(sel)
185		if out.OK || out.Kind != OutcomeConflict ||
186			out.Expected != 1 || out.Actual != 2 || out.Revision != 2 {
187			t.Fatalf("stale revision must conflict with both revisions: %+v", out)
188		}
189		if !strings.Contains(out.Reason, "revision 2, not 1") {
190			t.Fatalf("conflict reason must state both revisions, got %q", out.Reason)
191		}
192		assertNoTarget(out)
193	
194		// The correct revision with every healthy instance excluded is no_healthy;
195		// the reason says the exclusion removed them all.
196		out = selectExcluding(t, r, "svc", 2, nil, "a", "c", "d")
197		if out.OK || out.Kind != OutcomeNoHealthy || out.Revision != 2 {
198			t.Fatalf("excluding every healthy instance must be no_healthy at the current revision: %+v", out)
199		}
200		if !strings.Contains(out.Reason, "excludeInstanceIds") {
201			t.Fatalf("no_healthy reason must say the exclusion removed every healthy instance, got %q", out.Reason)
202		}
203		assertNoTarget(out)
204	
205		// Both failures left the cursor on the removed b: the next valid selection
206		// continues just after it and picks c — not d, which would mean skipping
207		// the instance that was due, and not a, which would mean restarting from
208		// the smallest id.
209		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 2), "c", "h3:3", 13)
210		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 2), "d", "h4:4", 14)
211	}

1	package indexroom
2	
3	import "testing"
4	
5	// This file is the regression guard for several session keys interleaved
6	// against ONE service. The per-service session map already binds each trimmed
7	// key independently, but the earlier suite only exercised a single key per
8	// service (or the same key in different services). These tests lock the
9	// cross-session guarantees purely through the public registration, health and
10	// selection results:
11	//
12	//   - two distinct keys first succeed by consuming the same rotation in turn,
13	//     each remembering its own instance; an existing binding never chooses the
14	//     target for a new key;
15	//   - interleaved keyed reuses return each session's own current binding
16	//     (id, address and latest accepted health sequence) without moving the
17	//     shared rotation, and plain selects continue from the last real rotation;
18	//   - when one key's bound instance turns unhealthy, only that key's binding is
19	//     rewritten by a fallback rotation, and two keys may legitimately bind to
20	//     the same instance without stealing each other's binding;
21	//   - an all-unhealthy no_healthy failure fabricates no target and preserves
22	//     both sessions' bindings and the rotation position.
23	//
24	// No session query, release or expiry operation exists or is introduced: the
25	// bindings are observed only through what later selections return.
26	
27	// selectSession validates and runs one select carrying a session key,
28	// returning the outcome (success or failure) so failure cases can be asserted
29	// directly instead of failing the helper.
30	func selectSession(t *testing.T, r *Registry, service string, revision int64, key string) SelectOutcome {
31		t.Helper()
32		sel, err := r.ValidateSelectionWithSession(service, revision, &key)
33		if err != nil {
34			t.Fatalf("validate select %s key %q: %v", service, key, err)
35		}
36		return r.Select(sel)
37	}
38	
39	// assertPick locks one successful selection's full target triple: instance id,
40	// current address and the instance's currently accepted health sequence must
41	// all belong to the same instance chosen for this request.
42	func assertPick(t *testing.T, out SelectOutcome, id, addr string, seq int64) {
43		t.Helper()
44		if !out.OK {
45			t.Fatalf("select should succeed, got %+v", out)
46		}
47		if out.InstanceID != id || out.Address != addr || out.Sequence != seq {
48			t.Fatalf("select target = %q/%s/seq %d, want %q/%s/seq %d (outcome %+v)",
49				out.InstanceID, out.Address, out.Sequence, id, addr, seq, out)
50		}
51	}
52	
53	// TestRegistryTwoSessionsShareOneRotationAndStayIndependent fixes the
54	// interleaving contract for two keys in one service. Both keys' first
55	// successes consume the same rotation in input order; later reuses never move
56	// it; plain selections continue just after the last instance an actual
57	// rotation returned; and every result carries the selected instance's own
58	// address and sequence rather than the other session's.
59	func TestRegistryTwoSessionsShareOneRotationAndStayIndependent(t *testing.T) {
60		r := NewRegistry()
61		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
62			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
63		})
64		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
65		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 2, true, "")
66		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 3, true, "")
67	
68		// The first key rotates from the unset position to the smallest id and
69		// binds x -> a; the shared cursor rests on a.
70		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
71	
72		// The second key is a different session: the existing x -> a binding must
73		// not pick its target. Its first success continues the SAME rotation from
74		// the current position, landing on b, and binds y -> b.
75		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
76	
77		// Interleaved reuses return each session's own binding and move nothing.
78		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
79		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
80	
81		// A plain select continues just after the last rotated id (b), proving the
82		// reuses above neither advanced nor rewound the rotation.
83		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "c", "h3:3", 3)
84	
85		// Reusing the earlier-bound instance (a) must not drag a later plain select
86		// backwards, and the other session's reuse must not skip a healthy
87		// instance: both reuses still answer their own bindings while the cursor
88		// stays on c.
89		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
90		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
91	
92		// Plain rotation wraps past c to a, then continues to b exactly once each:
93		// no reuse inserted an extra skip.
94		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 1)
95		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "b", "h2:2", 2)
96	
97		// Newer accepted observations on the bound instances are reflected per
98		// session: x reports a's current record and y reports b's, never a mix.
99		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 10, true, "")
100		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 20, true, "")
101		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 10)
102		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 20)
103	
104		// The plain rotation is still where the last real rotation left it (b), so
105		// it continues to c and then wraps to a carrying a's latest sequence.
106		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "c", "h3:3", 3)
107		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 10)
108	
109		// Selections changed neither the revision nor any accepted health record.
110		if rev := r.RevisionOf("svc"); rev != 1 {
111			t.Fatalf("selection changed the registration revision: %d", rev)
112		}
113		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "a"); inst.Health != HealthHealthy || inst.Sequence != 10 || inst.Reason != "" {
114			t.Fatalf("a accepted record changed by selection: %+v", inst)
115		}
116		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "b"); inst.Health != HealthHealthy || inst.Sequence != 20 {
117			t.Fatalf("b accepted record changed by selection: %+v", inst)
118		}
119		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "c"); inst.Health != HealthHealthy || inst.Sequence != 3 {
120			t.Fatalf("c accepted record changed by selection: %+v", inst)
121		}
122	}
123	
124	// TestRegistrySessionUnhealthyRebindIsolatesAndMayShare drives one session's
125	// bound instance unhealthy while another session's instance stays healthy. The
126	// affected session alone reselects from the current rotation and rewrites only
127	// its own binding; the two sessions are then allowed to converge on the same
128	// instance without it being a conflict or stealing the other binding. The
129	// originally bound instance recovering afterwards does not move the rebound
130	// session, and a plain select continues from the successful reselection's
131	// position.
132	func TestRegistrySessionUnhealthyRebindIsolatesAndMayShare(t *testing.T) {
133		r := NewRegistry()
134		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
135			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
136		})

139		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 3, true, "")

143		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)

146		// remain healthy.
147		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 4, false, "down")
148	
149		// x's next selection cannot reuse a and falls back to the rotation at its
150		// current position (just after b), choosing c. Only x's binding moves; the
151		// returned triple is c's, never stale data from a.
152		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "c", "h3:3", 3)
153

155		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
156		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "c", "h3:3", 3)
157

159		// instance. x's fallback continues just after c, wraps and rebinds to b.
160		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 5, false, "down")
161		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
162	
163		// Two different sessions bound to the same instance is allowed: it is not
164		// a conflict and neither request displaces the other session's binding.
165		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
166		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
167

169		// recovers. The session that moved (x) keeps reusing its new binding b;
170		// recovery never steals it back. The other session keeps its own binding.
171		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 6, true, "")
172		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
173		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)

177		// a's recovered sequence rather than restarting at a's old record.

181		// answer b even though the cursor moved through a.
182		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
183		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
184	
185		// The selections and binding changes left the revision and the accepted
186		// health records exactly as the observations set them.
187		if rev := r.RevisionOf("svc"); rev != 1 {
188			t.Fatalf("selection changed the registration revision: %d", rev)
189		}
190		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "a"); inst.Health != HealthHealthy || inst.Sequence != 6 || inst.Reason != "" {
191			t.Fatalf("a final record: %+v", inst)
192		}
193		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "b"); inst.Health != HealthHealthy || inst.Sequence != 2 {
194			t.Fatalf("b final record: %+v", inst)
195		}
196		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "c"); inst.Health != HealthUnhealthy || inst.Sequence != 5 || inst.Reason != "down" {
197			t.Fatalf("c final record: %+v", inst)
198		}
199	}

201	// TestRegistryTwoSessionsNoHealthyKeepsBothBindingsAndCursor isolates the
202	// failure path shared by two sessions: once every instance is unhealthy, keyed
203	// and plain selections all return no_healthy with the current revision and a
204	// reason but no fabricated instance, address or sequence. The failures
205	// preserve both sessions' prior bindings and the shared rotation position.
206	//
207	// Recovery is ordered so a surviving binding is distinguishable from a fresh
208	// rotation: an instance no session is bound to (c) recovers first, then x's
209	// bound a recovers while the cursor still rests on b. A request that reused
210	// the preserved binding returns a; one that had lost it would rotate just
211	// after b to c instead. After y's bound b recovers both sessions reuse their
212	// own targets with the latest sequences, and a plain select resumes from the
213	// last real rotation at c rather than anywhere the failures or reuses moved.
214	func TestRegistryTwoSessionsNoHealthyKeepsBothBindingsAndCursor(t *testing.T) {
215		r := NewRegistry()
216		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
217			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
218		})
219		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 1, true, "")
220		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 2, true, "")
221		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 3, true, "")
222	
223		// x -> a then y -> b; the last real rotation parked the shared cursor on b.
224		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 1)
225		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 2)
226	
227		// Every instance receives a newer unhealthy observation.
228		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 4, false, "down")
229		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 5, false, "down")
230		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 6, false, "down")
231	
232		// Keyed and plain requests all fail the same way: no_healthy at the
233		// current revision with a stated reason, inventing neither an instance id
234		// nor an address nor a sequence.
235		assertNoHealthy := func(key *string) {
236			t.Helper()
237			var out SelectOutcome
238			if key == nil {
239				sel, err := r.ValidateSelection("svc", 1)
240				if err != nil {
241					t.Fatalf("validate plain select: %v", err)
242				}
243				out = r.Select(sel)
244			} else {
245				out = selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, *key)
246			}
247			if out.OK || out.Kind != OutcomeNoHealthy {
248				t.Fatalf("should be no_healthy, got %+v", out)
249			}
250			if out.Revision != 1 || out.Reason == "" {
251				t.Fatalf("no_healthy must state revision and reason, got %+v", out)
252			}
253			if out.InstanceID != "" || out.Address != "" || out.Sequence != 0 {
254				t.Fatalf("no_healthy must fabricate no target, got id=%q addr=%q seq=%d", out.InstanceID, out.Address, out.Sequence)
255			}
256		}
257		keyX, keyY := "x", "y"
258		assertNoHealthy(&keyX)
259		assertNoHealthy(&keyY)
260		assertNoHealthy(nil)
261	
262		// An instance no session is bound to recovers first. No keyed request is
263		// made against it: it only establishes a healthy rotation candidate past
264		// the cursor so a later fresh rotation would not coincide with x's binding.
265		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 7, true, "")
266	
267		// x's own bound instance a recovers while b is still down. x reuses a
268		// directly with its latest sequence: had the failure erased the binding,
269		// this would be a first-time rotation from cursor b, which skips past b to
270		// c — returning a therefore proves the preserved binding was reused and
271		// the rotation never moved.
272		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "a", 1, 8, true, "")
273		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 8)
274	
275		// y's bound instance b recovers; y likewise reuses b directly instead of
276		// rotating to c, showing its binding survived too.
277		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 9, true, "")
278		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 9)
279		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 8)
280	
281		// The last real rotation is still y's original success on b; all the
282		// no_healthy failures and direct reuses left the cursor there. A plain
283		// select therefore continues just after b to c, then wraps through a and b
284		// using each instance's recovered sequence.
285		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "c", "h3:3", 7)
286		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "a", "h1:1", 8)
287		assertPick(t, selected(t, r, "svc", 1), "b", "h2:2", 9)
288	
289		// The plain rotation rewrote no session binding: both sessions still
290		// answer their own targets.
291		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "x"), "a", "h1:1", 8)
292		assertPick(t, selectSession(t, r, "svc", 1, "y"), "b", "h2:2", 9)
293	
294		// Neither the failed selections nor the successful reuses changed a
295		// revision or an accepted health record.
296		if rev := r.RevisionOf("svc"); rev != 1 {
297			t.Fatalf("failures changed the registration revision: %d", rev)
298		}
299		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "a"); inst.Health != HealthHealthy || inst.Sequence != 8 || inst.Reason != "" {
300			t.Fatalf("a final record: %+v", inst)
301		}
302		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "b"); inst.Health != HealthHealthy || inst.Sequence != 9 || inst.Reason != "" {
303			t.Fatalf("b final record: %+v", inst)
304		}
305		if inst := instanceHealth(t, r, "svc", "c"); inst.Health != HealthHealthy || inst.Sequence != 7 || inst.Reason != "" {
306			t.Fatalf("c final record: %+v", inst)
307		}
308	}

1	// Command indexroom is the 链上索引与交易分析服务 entry point.
2	package main
3	
4	import (
5		"encoding/json"
6		"fmt"
7		"io"
8		"os"
9		"strings"
10	
11		"github.com/gzhysuiioo/indexroom-analytics/indexroom"
12	)
13	
14	func main() {
15		command := "demo"
16		if len(os.Args) > 1 {
17			command = os.Args[1]
18		}
19		switch command {
20		case "demo":
21			runDemo()
22		case "version":
23			fmt.Println("indexroom 0.1.0")
24		case "register":
25			// register reports result-delivery failures via its exit status and
26			// stderr; a broken standard output must surface as an EPIPE write error,
27			// not as the default SIGPIPE termination.
28			ignoreSigpipe()
29			os.Exit(runRegister())
30		case "help", "-h", "--help":
31			usage()
32		default:
33			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unknown command %q\n", command)
34			usage()
35			os.Exit(2)
36		}
37	}
38	
39	func usage() {
40		fmt.Println("usage: indexroom [demo|version|register|help]")
41		fmt.Println()
42		fmt.Println("register reads requests as JSON from standard input and maintains an")
43		fmt.Println("in-memory service instance registry with offline health observations:")
44		fmt.Println(`  {"requests":[{"type":"register","service":"svc","expectedRevision":0,"instances":[{"id":"i1","address":"host:8080"}]},`)
45		fmt.Println(`              {"type":"health","service":"svc","instanceId":"i1","expectedRevision":1,"sequence":1,"healthy":true},`)
46		fmt.Println(`              {"type":"select","service":"svc","expectedRevision":1},`)
47		fmt.Println(`              {"type":"release_session","service":"svc","expectedRevision":1,"sessionKey":"user-42"}]}`)
48		fmt.Println("A register request fully replaces the service's instance list; new services")
49		fmt.Println("require expectedRevision 0, existing services the current revision. A health")
50		fmt.Println("request records an offline observation (healthy/unhealthy) for one instance;")
51		fmt.Println("it never probes. Health updates never bump the registration revision. A")
52		fmt.Println("select request chooses one healthy instance, rotating per service by ascending")
53		fmt.Println("instance id; it performs no network access and never changes revisions or")
54		fmt.Println("health records, and reports invalid/conflict/not_found/no_healthy on failure.")
55		fmt.Println("A select request may carry an optional \"sessionKey\" string: requests in the")
56		fmt.Println("same service with the same trimmed key reuse the instance first chosen for")
57		fmt.Println("that key while it stays registered and healthy, without moving the rotation.")
58		fmt.Println("A select request may also carry an optional \"excludeInstanceIds\" array of")
59		fmt.Println("strings: the listed instances are skipped for that one request only, keeping")
60		fmt.Println("their registration and health records, and stay eligible for later requests.")
61		fmt.Println("A release_session request carries service, expectedRevision and a required")
62		fmt.Println("sessionKey; it drops that key's binding in the named service so the next")
63		fmt.Println("selection with the key joins the rotation again. It chooses no target, moves")
64		fmt.Println("no cursor, and succeeds without changed when the key has no binding.")
65		fmt.Println("Exit status is 0 only when every request succeeds and the JSON result")
66		fmt.Println("is fully written to standard output. A failed result write is reported")
67		fmt.Println("on standard error with the underlying write error and also exits 1,")
68		fmt.Println("without appending a second JSON document to the partial output.")
69	}
70	
71	// registerInstance is one instance in the final service list.
72	type registerInstance struct {
73		ID       string `json:"id"`
74		Address  string `json:"address"`
75		Health   string `json:"health"`
76		Sequence int64  `json:"sequence"`
77		Reason   string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
78	}
79	
80	// registerService is one service in the final service list.
81	type registerService struct {
82		Service   string             `json:"service"`
83		Revision  int                `json:"revision"`
84		Instances []registerInstance `json:"instances"`
85	}
86	
87	// registerResult is the per-item outcome.
88	type registerResult struct {
89		Service          string `json:"service"`
90		OK               bool   `json:"ok"`
91		Changed          bool   `json:"changed,omitempty"`
92		Revision         int    `json:"revision"`
93		Error            string `json:"error,omitempty"`
94		Reason           string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
95		ExpectedRevision int    `json:"expectedRevision,omitempty"`
96		ActualRevision   int    `json:"actualRevision,omitempty"`
97		Sequence         int64  `json:"sequence,omitempty"`
98		InstanceID       string `json:"instanceId,omitempty"`
99		Address          string `json:"address,omitempty"`
100	}
101	
102	// registerOutput is the full register output.
103	type registerOutput struct {
104		Results  []registerResult  `json:"results"`
105		Services []registerService `json:"services"`
106	}
107	
108	// runRegister processes registration requests from the process standard
109	// streams. It returns the process exit code: 0 when all registrations succeed
110	// and the result is fully written, 1 otherwise.
111	func runRegister() int {
112		return runRegisterIO(os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr)
113	}
114	
115	// runRegisterIO is runRegister with injectable streams. in supplies the JSON
116	// request batch, out receives the single JSON result document and errOut
117	// receives diagnostics (in particular a result-delivery failure, which must
118	// never be mixed into out).
119	func runRegisterIO(in io.Reader, out io.Writer, errOut io.Writer) int {
120		data, err := io.ReadAll(in)
121		if err != nil {
122			return failRegister(out, errOut, fmt.Sprintf("could not read standard input: %v", err))
123		}
124	
125		var top struct {
126			Requests json.RawMessage `json:"requests"`
127		}
128		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &top); err != nil {
129			return failRegister(out, errOut, fmt.Sprintf("input must be a JSON object with a requests array: %v", err))
130		}
131		if len(top.Requests) == 0 || strings.TrimSpace(string(top.Requests)) == "null" {
132			return failRegister(out, errOut, "input must contain a \"requests\" array")
133		}
134		var rawRequests []json.RawMessage
135		if err := json.Unmarshal(top.Requests, &rawRequests); err != nil {
136			return failRegister(out, errOut, "\"requests\" must be a JSON array")
137		}
138	
139		proc := &registerProcessor{
140			registry: indexroom.NewRegistry(),
141			results:  make([]registerResult, 0, len(rawRequests)),
142		}
143	
144		for _, raw := range rawRequests {
145			var head struct {
146				Service string          `json:"service"`
147				Type    json.RawMessage `json:"type"`
148			}
149			_ = json.Unmarshal(raw, &head)
150			service := strings.TrimSpace(head.Service)
151	
152			reqType := "register"
153			if len(head.Type) > 0 && strings.TrimSpace(string(head.Type)) != "null" {
154				var t string
155				if err := json.Unmarshal(head.Type, &t); err != nil {
156					proc.invalid(service, "type must be a string")
157					continue
158				}
159				reqType = t
160			}
161	
162			switch reqType {
163			case "", "register":
164				proc.registerRequest(raw, service)
165			case "health":
166				proc.healthRequest(raw, service)
167			case "select":
168				proc.selectRequest(raw, service)
169			case "release_session":
170				proc.releaseSessionRequest(raw, service)
171			default:
172				proc.invalidf(service, "unknown type %q", reqType)
173			}
174		}
175	
176		results, anyFailed := proc.results, proc.failed
177		registry := proc.registry
178	
179		services := make([]registerService, 0)
180		for _, view := range registry.Snapshot() {
181			insts := make([]registerInstance, 0, len(view.Instances))
182			for _, inst := range view.Instances {
183				insts = append(insts, registerInstance{
184					ID:       inst.ID,
185					Address:  inst.Address,
186					Health:   string(inst.Health),
187					Sequence: inst.Sequence,
188					Reason:   inst.Reason,
189				})
190			}
191			services = append(services, registerService{
192				Service:   view.Service,
193				Revision:  view.Revision,
194				Instances: insts,
195			})
196		}
197	
198		if err := writeRegisterOutput(out, registerOutput{Results: results, Services: services}); err != nil {
199			// The request results could not be delivered. This is independent of
200			// whether the requests themselves succeeded: the caller must be able to
201			// tell an undelivered result from a rejected request.
202			reportRegisterDeliveryFailure(errOut, err)
203			return 1
204		}
205		if anyFailed {
206			return 1
207		}
208		return 0
209	}
210	
211	// registerProcessor runs the request batch in input order. Failed items keep
212	// their slot in results and set failed; later items still run against the
213	// state committed by earlier successful items.
214	type registerProcessor struct {
215		registry *indexroom.Registry
216		results  []registerResult
217		failed   bool
218	}
219	
220	// invalid records an input-validation failure for an item. Content validity is
221	// checked before any business rule, so the revision stamped here is the
222	// service's current revision when the item is handled.
223	func (p *registerProcessor) invalid(service, reason string) {
224		p.failed = true
225		p.results = append(p.results, registerResult{
226			Service:  service,
227			OK:       false,
228			Error:    "invalid",
229			Reason:   reason,
230			Revision: p.registry.RevisionOf(service),
231		})
232	}
233	
234	// invalidf is invalid with a formatted reason.
235	func (p *registerProcessor) invalidf(service, format string, args ...any) {
236		p.invalid(service, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))
237	}
238	
239	// revisionMissing reports whether a raw expectedRevision token is absent or
240	// explicitly null; both report the shared required-field error.
241	func revisionMissing(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
242		return len(raw) == 0 || strings.TrimSpace(string(raw)) == "null"
243	}
244	
245	// parseRevision decodes the raw expectedRevision token for one request. An
246	// absent or explicitly null token is "required"; a token that is not a decimal
247	// integer is an integer-type invalid. A decimal integer is returned as int64 —
248	// still carrying the submitted value — so the registry can range-check it
249	// against the architecture (0..2147483647 on 32-bit, 0..9223372036854775807
250	// on 64-bit) before it is narrowed to int; narrowing first would wrap values
251	// like 4294967297 into 1 on a 32-bit build. It reports false after appending
252	// the item's invalid result, which stamps the service's current revision.
253	// Every request kind shares this check, so the missing/null reason and its
254	// precedence live here rather than at each call site.
255	func (p *registerProcessor) parseRevision(service string, raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
256		if revisionMissing(raw) {
257			p.invalid(service, "expectedRevision is required and must be a non-negative integer")
258			return 0, false
259		}
260		revision, err := indexroom.ParseExpectedRevision(string(raw))
261		if err != nil {
262			p.invalid(service, err.Error())
263			return 0, false
264		}
265		return revision, true
266	}
267	
268	// parseSequence decodes the raw sequence token for one health observation. A
269	// decimal integer is returned as int64 carrying the submitted value exactly;
270	// a non-integer token (a float, string or boolean) and a magnitude outside
271	// the signed int64 range — including 9223372036854775808, one past the
272	// maximum — become that item's own invalid result with a reason naming the
273	// sequence problem, instead of failing the whole item's JSON decode with a
274	// Go-level unmarshal error. Reading the token raw is what keeps the batch
275	// per-item: one out-of-range sequence neither aborts the batch nor steals the
276	// outcomes of later items. The positive-value rule is enforced afterwards by
277	// the registry's ValidateHealth, alongside its other content checks.
278	func (p *registerProcessor) parseSequence(service string, raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
279		sequence, err := indexroom.ParseSequence(string(raw))
280		if err != nil {
281			p.invalid(service, err.Error())
282			return 0, false
283		}
284		return sequence, true
285	}
286	
287	// sessionRequestInput is the decoded content shared by select and
288	// release_session requests: the trimmed service name, the parsed
289	// expectedRevision (still int64, range-checked later by the registry before it
290	// is narrowed to int), and the optional session key (nil when the field was
291	// omitted). Explicit null and non-string keys are rejected while decoding.
292	// excludeIDs is the raw excludeInstanceIds token, kept undecoded here: only
293	// select interprets it, and its per-element checks live with the select
294	// handler so release_session keeps ignoring the field.
295	type sessionRequestInput struct {
296		service    string
297		revision   int64
298		sessionKey *string
299		excludeIDs json.RawMessage
300	}
301	
302	// readSessionRequest decodes one select/release_session item, centralizing the
303	// input handling the two request kinds repeat. shapeReason is the operation's
304	// format string for a malformed object (it consumes the decode error).
305	//
306	// The field order is the one every request kind keeps: a missing or null
307	// expectedRevision is the required-field error first; once the revision token
308	// is present, an explicit null or a non-string sessionKey is the sessionKey
309	// type error (never "no key submitted"), and only then is the revision parsed
310	// as an integer. An omitted sessionKey arrives as nil: select's validator
311	// treats it as an ordinary rotating selection, while release_session's
312	// validator rejects it as a sessionKey problem — each after the service-name
313	// and revision-range checks, so a simultaneously bad revision still precedes
314	// it. A present string key is trimmed by the registry's shared validator
315	// together with that range check: keys equal after trimming name one session
316	// and a blank-after-trim key loses to nothing but a service-name or
317	// revision-range problem. On failure the item's invalid result is appended and
318	// ok is false; on success the caller validates against the registry and maps
319	// its own business outcome.
320	func (p *registerProcessor) readSessionRequest(raw json.RawMessage, service, shapeReason string) (sessionRequestInput, bool) {
321		var req struct {
322			Service  string          `json:"service"`
323			Revision json.RawMessage `json:"expectedRevision"`
324			Session  json.RawMessage `json:"sessionKey"`
325			Exclude  json.RawMessage `json:"excludeInstanceIds"`
326		}
327		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &req); err != nil {
328			p.invalidf(service, shapeReason, err)
329			return sessionRequestInput{}, false
330		}
331		service = strings.TrimSpace(req.Service)
332	
333		if revisionMissing(req.Revision) {
334			p.invalid(service, "expectedRevision is required and must be a non-negative integer")
335			return sessionRequestInput{}, false
336		}
337	
338		// An explicit null or a non-string token names a sessionKey type problem
339		// for either request kind; it is judged once the revision token is known
340		// present and before the revision is parsed. An omitted field stays nil and
341		// reaches the operation's own validator, which distinguishes an ordinary
342		// keyless select from release_session's mandatory key.
343		var sessionKey *string
344		if len(req.Session) > 0 {
345			if strings.TrimSpace(string(req.Session)) == "null" {
346				p.invalid(service, "sessionKey must be a string, not null")
347				return sessionRequestInput{}, false
348			}
349			var key string
350			if err := json.Unmarshal(req.Session, &key); err != nil {
351				p.invalid(service, "sessionKey must be a string")
352				return sessionRequestInput{}, false
353			}
354			sessionKey = &key
355		}
356	
357		revision, ok := p.parseRevision(service, req.Revision)
358		if !ok {
359			return sessionRequestInput{}, false
360		}
361		return sessionRequestInput{service: service, revision: revision, sessionKey: sessionKey, excludeIDs: req.Exclude}, true
362	}
363	
364	// parseExcludeIDs decodes the raw excludeInstanceIds token of one select
365	// request. An omitted field (and only that) yields a nil list, which selects
366	// exactly as before; an explicit null, a non-array token or a non-string
367	// element becomes this item's own invalid result with a reason naming the
368	// excludeInstanceIds problem, so one malformed list neither aborts the batch
369	// nor partially applies alongside the valid ids it also carried. The elements
370	// are returned as submitted — trimming, deduplication and the blank-id rule
371	// belong to the registry's validator, which runs them before any revision
372	// comparison just like the sessionKey checks. It reports false after
373	// appending the item's invalid result, which stamps the service's current
374	// revision.
375	func (p *registerProcessor) parseExcludeIDs(service string, raw json.RawMessage) ([]string, bool) {
376		if len(raw) == 0 {
377			return nil, true
378		}
379		if strings.TrimSpace(string(raw)) == "null" {
380			p.invalid(service, "excludeInstanceIds must be an array of strings, not null")

384			p.invalid(service, "excludeInstanceIds must be an array of strings")
385			return nil, false

390			return nil, false

408	func (p *registerProcessor) reject(service string, kind indexroom.OutcomeKind, reason string, revision, expected, actual int, sequence int64) {
409		p.failed = true
410		p.results = append(p.results, registerResult{
411			Service:          service,
412			OK:               false,
413			Error:            string(kind),
414			Reason:           reason,
415			Revision:         revision,
416			ExpectedRevision: expected,
417			ActualRevision:   actual,
418			Sequence:         sequence,

423	// the output exactly as before the refactor.
424	func (p *registerProcessor) succeed(result registerResult) {
425		result.OK = true
426		p.results = append(p.results, result)

429	// registerRequest processes one register request, appending its outcome.
430	func (p *registerProcessor) registerRequest(raw json.RawMessage, service string) {
431		var req struct {
432			Service   string          `json:"service"`
433			Revision  json.RawMessage `json:"expectedRevision"`
434			Instances json.RawMessage `json:"instances"`
435		}
436		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &req); err != nil {
437			p.invalidf(service, "request must be an object with service, expectedRevision and instances: %v", err)
438			return
439		}
440		service = strings.TrimSpace(req.Service)
441	
442		if revisionMissing(req.Revision) {
443			p.invalid(service, "expectedRevision is required and must be a non-negative integer")
444			return
445		}
446		if !isJSONArray(req.Instances) {
447			p.invalid(service, "instances must be an array")
448			return
449		}
450		var instances []indexroom.Instance
451		if err := json.Unmarshal(req.Instances, &instances); err != nil {
452			p.invalidf(service, "instances must be an array of objects with id and address: %v", err)
453			return
454		}
455	
456		// Parse the raw token (integer type); ValidateRegistration then range-checks
457		// the int64 against the architecture before narrowing it to int.
458		revision, ok := p.parseRevision(service, req.Revision)
459		if !ok {
460			return
461		}
462		registration, err := p.registry.ValidateRegistration(service, revision, instances)
463		if err != nil {
464			p.invalid(service, err.Error())
465			return
466		}
467	
468		outcome := p.registry.Apply(registration)
469		if !outcome.OK {
470			p.reject(outcome.Service, outcome.Kind, outcome.Reason, outcome.Revision, outcome.Expected, outcome.Actual, 0)
471			return
472		}
473		p.succeed(registerResult{
474			Service:  outcome.Service,
475			Changed:  outcome.Changed,
476			Revision: outcome.Revision,
477		})
478	}

480	// healthRequest processes one health observation request, appending its outcome.
481	func (p *registerProcessor) healthRequest(raw json.RawMessage, service string) {
482		var req struct {
483			Service    string          `json:"service"`
484			InstanceID string          `json:"instanceId"`
485			Revision   json.RawMessage `json:"expectedRevision"`
486			Sequence   json.RawMessage `json:"sequence"`
487			Healthy    *bool           `json:"healthy"`
488			Reason     *string         `json:"reason"`
489		}
490		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &req); err != nil {
491			p.invalidf(service, "health request must be an object with service, instanceId, expectedRevision, sequence and healthy: %v", err)
492			return
493		}
494		service = strings.TrimSpace(req.Service)
495	
496		if revisionMissing(req.Revision) {
497			p.invalid(service, "expectedRevision is required and must be a non-negative integer")
498			return
499		}
500		if len(req.Sequence) == 0 || strings.TrimSpace(string(req.Sequence)) == "null" {
501			p.invalid(service, "sequence is required and must be a positive integer")
502			return
503		}
504		if req.Healthy == nil {
505			p.invalid(service, "healthy is required and must be a boolean")
506			return
507		}
508		reason := ""
509		if req.Reason != nil {
510			reason = *req.Reason
511		}
512	
513		// Parse the raw tokens (integer type); ValidateHealth then range-checks
514		// the revision against the architecture before narrowing it to int, while
515		// a non-integer or out-of-range sequence becomes this item's own invalid
516		// result carrying a sequence-specific reason rather than a decode error.
517		revision, ok := p.parseRevision(service, req.Revision)
518		if !ok {
519			return
520		}
521		sequence, ok := p.parseSequence(service, req.Sequence)
522		if !ok {
523			return
524		}
525		update, err := p.registry.ValidateHealth(service, req.InstanceID, revision, sequence, *req.Healthy, reason)
526		if err != nil {
527			p.invalid(service, err.Error())
528			return
529		}
530	
531		outcome := p.registry.ApplyHealth(update)
532		if !outcome.OK {
533			p.reject(outcome.Service, outcome.Kind, outcome.Reason, outcome.Revision, outcome.Expected, outcome.Actual, outcome.Sequence)
534			return
535		}
536		p.succeed(registerResult{
537			Service:  outcome.Service,
538			Changed:  outcome.Changed,
539			Revision: outcome.Revision,
540			Sequence: outcome.Sequence,
541		})

544	// selectRequest processes one select request, appending its outcome.
545	// A selection performs no network access and never alters registrations or
546	// health records; it only advances the service's healthy-instance rotation
547	// and, for requests carrying a sessionKey, maintains that session's binding.
548	// An optional excludeInstanceIds array of strings skips the listed instances
549	// for this one request without touching their registration or health records.
550	func (p *registerProcessor) selectRequest(raw json.RawMessage, service string) {
551		in, ok := p.readSessionRequest(raw, service,
552			"select request must be an object with service and expectedRevision: %v")
553		if !ok {
554			return
555		}
556	
557		// The exclude list is decoded after the shared session/revision token
558		// handling and validated by the registry before any revision comparison,
559		// so a malformed list is this item's own invalid result and never a
560		// conflict, and the valid ids it also carried cannot partially apply.
561		excludeIDs, ok := p.parseExcludeIDs(in.service, in.excludeIDs)
562		if !ok {
563			return
564		}
565	
566		// readSessionRequest delivered the parsed revision and the key as decoded
567		// (nil for an omitted key); ValidateSelectionWithExclusions repeats the
568		// shared service/revision/key content checks via the registry, trims the
569		// key, and normalizes the exclude list (trimming, deduplicating and
570		// rejecting blank ids).
571		selection, err := p.registry.ValidateSelectionWithExclusions(in.service, in.revision, in.sessionKey, excludeIDs)
572		if err != nil {
573			p.invalid(in.service, err.Error())
574			return
575		}
576	
577		outcome := p.registry.Select(selection)
578		if !outcome.OK {
579			p.reject(outcome.Service, outcome.Kind, outcome.Reason, outcome.Revision, outcome.Expected, outcome.Actual, 0)
580			return
581		}
582		p.succeed(registerResult{
583			Service:    outcome.Service,
584			Revision:   outcome.Revision,
585			InstanceID: outcome.InstanceID,
586			Address:    outcome.Address,
587			Sequence:   outcome.Sequence,
588		})
589	}

591	// releaseSessionRequest processes one release_session request, appending its
592	// outcome. The request releases one session binding in one service: it never
593	// selects a target, never moves the rotation cursor or any other binding, and
594	// never alters the instance list, revision or health records. A present
595	// binding is removed and reported changed; releasing an unbound key still
596	// succeeds without changed.
597	func (p *registerProcessor) releaseSessionRequest(raw json.RawMessage, service string) {
598		in, ok := p.readSessionRequest(raw, service,
599			"release_session request must be an object with service, expectedRevision and sessionKey: %v")
600		if !ok {
601			return
602		}
603	
604		// The key is mandatory for release: readSessionRequest rejects an explicit
605		// null or non-string key, and an omitted key reaches ValidateSessionRelease
606		// as nil and is rejected there after the service-name and revision-range
607		// checks. The validator also trims the key and rejects a blank one before
608		// any revision comparison against the registry.
609		release, err := p.registry.ValidateSessionRelease(in.service, in.revision, in.sessionKey)
610		if err != nil {
611			p.invalid(in.service, err.Error())
612			return
613		}
614	
615		outcome := p.registry.ReleaseSession(release)
616		if !outcome.OK {
617			p.reject(outcome.Service, outcome.Kind, outcome.Reason, outcome.Revision, outcome.Expected, outcome.Actual, 0)
618			return
619		}
620		p.succeed(registerResult{
621			Service:  outcome.Service,
622			Changed:  outcome.Changed,
623			Revision: outcome.Revision,
624		})
625	}

627	// failRegister emits a top-level input error as the single JSON document on
628	// out and returns exit code 1. If that error JSON itself cannot be written,
629	// the delivery failure is diagnosed on errOut (out may already hold a partial
630	// document, so no second JSON is appended) and the exit code stays 1.
631	func failRegister(out io.Writer, errOut io.Writer, reason string) int {
632		if err := writeRegisterOutput(out, struct {
633			Error string `json:"error"`
634		}{Error: reason}); err != nil {
635			reportRegisterDeliveryFailure(errOut, err)
636		}
637		return 1
638	}
639	
640	// reportRegisterDeliveryFailure reports on errOut that the register command's
641	// JSON result could not be delivered, preserving the underlying write error.
642	// It never writes to standard output, which may already contain a partial
643	// result.
644	func reportRegisterDeliveryFailure(errOut io.Writer, err error) {
645		fmt.Fprintf(errOut, "register: failed to write request results to standard output: %v\n", err)
646	}
647	
648	// writeRegisterOutput writes v as the single indented JSON document on w.
649	// Standard output is dedicated to this document, so a write failure is returned
650	// instead of swallowed: the caller must not attempt to append another document
651	// after a partial write.
652	func writeRegisterOutput(w io.Writer, v any) error {
653		enc := json.NewEncoder(w)
654		enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
655		return enc.Encode(v)
656	}

658	// isJSONArray reports whether raw is a JSON array (ignoring leading whitespace).
659	func isJSONArray(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
660		for _, b := range raw {
661			switch b {
662			case ' ', '\t', '\n', '\r':
663				continue
664			case '[':
665				return true
666			default:
667				return false
668			}
669		}
670		return false
671	}

8	// This file is the regression guard for the select request's optional
9	// excludeInstanceIds list. The list scopes one request only: excluded
10	// instances stay registered with their health records and remain eligible for
11	// later requests that carry no list. These tests lock the contract purely
12	// through the public validation, selection and snapshot results:
13	//
14	//   - the rotation still continues just after the last actually rotated id,
15	//     skipping excluded ids without resetting the position, and wraps to the
16	//     smallest candidate only when no candidate follows;
17	//   - a session whose bound instance is excluded falls back to the filtered
18	//     rotation and rebinds only its own key on success, while other sessions
19	//     keep their bindings;
20	//   - excluding every healthy instance is no_healthy with a reason naming the
21	//     exclusion, and failures move neither the cursor nor any binding;
22	//   - the list is trimmed and deduplicated, unknown ids are ignored, a blank
23	//     id is invalid naming excludeInstanceIds, and field validation precedes
24	//     the revision check.

26	// selectExcluding validates and runs one select carrying an excludeInstanceIds
27	// list (and optionally a session key), returning the outcome so failure cases
28	// can be asserted directly instead of failing the helper.
29	func selectExcluding(t *testing.T, r *Registry, service string, revision int64, key *string, excludes ...string) SelectOutcome {
30		t.Helper()
31		sel, err := r.ValidateSelectionWithExclusions(service, revision, key, excludes)
32		if err != nil {
33			t.Fatalf("validate select excludes %v: %v", excludes, err)
34		}
35		return r.Select(sel)
36	}

38	// TestRegistrySelectExcludeRotatesPastExcludedIDs locks the spec's rotation
39	// example: with the cursor resting on a and a, b, c all healthy, excluding b
40	// chooses c, the next plain selection wraps to a, and the one after chooses
41	// the previously excluded b — the exclusion neither resets the position nor
42	// removes the instance from later rotations.
43	func TestRegistrySelectExcludeRotatesPastExcludedIDs(t *testing.T) {
44		r := NewRegistry()
45		registerService(t, r, "svc", 0, []Instance{
46			{ID: "a", Address: "h1:1"}, {ID: "b", Address: "h2:2"}, {ID: "c", Address: "h3:3"},
47		})

49		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "b", 1, 2, true, "")
50		markHealth(t, r, "svc", "c", 1, 3, true, "")

56		// after a and lands on c.
